front: Why can't mlx-lm 0.32 run on the Python that came with the Mac?
back: It needs Python 3.11 or newer. The Mac came with 3.9.

front: In the name Qwen3.5-4B-4bit, what do 4B and 4bit mean?
back: About 4 billion parameters. Each weight stored in about 4 bits.
A little accuracy, for a model about a third of the size and memory.

front: A reasoning model returned no answer within the token limit. What happened?
back: Its thinking used the whole token budget. Raise the limit or turn thinking off.

front: Why download models only from accounts you can identify?
back: Impostor accounts publish altered copies under real model names.
Small added low-rank matrices. The original weights stay frozen.

front: What is in a LoRA adapter file?
back: Only the trained added weights. Megabytes, loaded on top of the unchanged base model.

front: Training loss fell. Does that prove the model got better at the task?
back: No. Only a held-out test set, scored before and after, can show that.
The score from always answering the most common label. Here: always "Health", 8.0% on the golden set.

front: Why are bills split by normalized title, not one by one?
back: Companion and reintroduced bills share titles. Splitting by title keeps a test title out of training.

front: Why is the golden set committed to git instead of rebuilt each time?
back: The public record changes daily. A frozen set makes every score comparable to every other.

front: What does a stratified test set guarantee?
back: Every label with enough examples appears, here at least twice, so rare labels are tested too.

front: How does the harness treat a reply it cannot parse into a label?
back: As invalid: counted wrong and reported separately. Never dropped, or dodging hard cases would raise accuracy.

front: What does macro-F1 add over accuracy?
back: It averages F1 across labels equally, so failing on a small label hurts as much as a big one.

front: Why is Qwen3.5's thinking turned off for this eval?
back: Thinking cost 1,500+ tokens and about 20 seconds per bill, and could run out of room before answering.

front: How is cost per 1,000 bills computed?
back: Measured input and output tokens times per-token prices given at run time, scaled to 1,000 bills.

front: Which error group can a fine-tune fix, and which can it not?
back: It can learn labelling conventions, like tax-code bills being Taxation. It cannot recover facts a thin title never states.

front: What does the CI gate check, given that it runs no model?
back: It re-scores committed predictions against the frozen golden labels and fails below the accuracy or above the invalid bar.

front: Why does the gate take gold labels from the golden file, not the predictions file?
back: So a predictions file cannot grade itself by rewriting its own gold labels.
